editorialHook: One university just cut their AI costs by 80% — and the model they used is something any campus could replicate.

deepDive.title: Boise State Builds Campus-Wide AI on AWS — At a Fraction of the Cost
deepDive.summary: Boise State's new AI platform gives every student and faculty member access to AI tools through a single portal. Built on AWS, they claim an 80% reduction in per-user costs compared to individual licenses. Here's how you could pitch something similar at your institution.

quickHits.title: Canva Adds AI-Powered Slide Generator for Educators
quickHits.summary: Canva's new feature lets you paste a syllabus and get a full slide deck. It's free for educators with a .edu email. Worth trying this week if you're prepping spring materials.

quickHits.title: Survey: 73% of Faculty Say They Need More AI Training
quickHits.summary: A new Educause survey puts a number on what many of us already knew — faculty want help with AI but aren't getting it. The gap between interest and institutional support is widening.

quickHits.title: Community College in Texas Launches Free AI Literacy Certificate
quickHits.summary: Austin Community College is offering a free, stackable AI literacy credential for both students and community members. A model worth watching for accessibility-focused institutions.

closingThought: The through-line today is access. Whether it's Boise State cutting costs to get AI into every student's hands, Canva making slide creation free, or a community college opening AI training to the public — the institutions getting ahead are the ones removing barriers, not adding them.
